summary: P2 Universal Multi-Country Fiscal Reports module backend regression: 14/14 tests PASSED. Validated /api/multi-country-reports/available-reports + /api/multi-country-reports/fiscal-summary (CSV + PDF). CSV adapts headers per country: DR(SFS/AFP + SRL/INFOTEP, DGII), CO(SALUD/PENSION + ARL/CCF/ICBF/SENA, DIAN), US(SS/MEDICARE + FUTA, IRS), ES(CC/DESEMPLEO/FP/FOGASA, AEAT), MX(IMSS, SAT). PDF returns valid %PDF- bytes >2KB. Filename Content-Disposition correctly carries country_code and period. period=YYYY-MM and period=period_id both supported. Errors: invalid format -> 400, non-existent period -> 404. DR-specific endpoints regression after country switches: tss/autodeterminacion, tss-report, tss-preview all 200. Company test_refactor@fortexa.com restored to DO at end (verified country_code=DO).
critical_code_review_comments: multi_country_reports.py is well-scoped (~400 lines), uses get_company_rates_flat() and COUNTRY_PROFILES from country_config.py — no duplication of country data. Good DRY.
Both _render_csv and _render_pdf dynamically build header columns from emp_deds_profile / er_conts_profile so any of the 28 country profiles works with zero hardcoding. Solid design.
CSV output is encoded as utf-8-sig (BOM) for Excel compatibility — appropriate for fiscal users.
PDF builds two stacked tables (employee deductions + employer contributions) in landscape A4 with clear styling and totals row highlighted. Adequate for fiscal reporting.

Note (expected per spec): DB amount values (sfs_employee, afp_employee, srl_employer, infotep_employer fields in payroll_entries) are populated from the country active at calculation time. After switching country the CSV labels reflect the NEW country but amounts come from the OLD calc. To get fully recalculated numbers users must re-run period calc. Confirmed by main agent as expected behavior.

Minor: in _sum_detail_for_entry only first 4 employer slots are read from DB (sfs_employer, afp_employer, srl_employer, infotep_employer). For countries with >4 employer contributions (e.g. CO has 6: SALUD/PENSION/ARL/CCF/ICBF/SENA), slots 5+ are computed on-the-fly from gross*rate. This is acceptable for header/label adaptation, but the 4 stored values use DR-style slot ordering — for countries where the first 4 slot semantics differ, displayed values may not match labels. This was flagged in the spec note; recommend documenting this on the endpoint or extending payroll_entries schema in a future iteration.
Available-reports endpoint correctly merges country-specific reports (profile.reports) with universal_reports list. Clean.

Pre-existing iter231 issue (dgii_reports.py:170 .replace on None) seems to no longer manifest — autodeterminacion returned 200 in this run. Either E1 fixed it or current employees have non-null document_number; verify by viewing the file.
